front: What is the ranking of irrigation sources in India by percentage of net irrigated area?
back:
1. Wells and Tube-wells (~62-64%)
2. Canals (~24-26%)
3. Tanks (~3-4%)
4. Other sources (~6-8%).

front: Which Indian state has the largest area under Tube-well irrigation?
back: Uttar Pradesh. It leads India in both total canal irrigated area and tube-well irrigated area.

front: Why is tank irrigation predominantly practiced in Peninsular India (South India)?
back:
1. Hard crystalline, impermeable rock terrain makes well-digging difficult.
2. Natural depressions easily store monsoon runoff.
3. Seasonal, non-perennial rivers limit perennial canal networks.

front: From which headworks/barrage does the Indira Gandhi Canal (Rajasthan Canal) originate?
back: Harike Barrage in Punjab, located at the confluence of the Sutlej and Beas rivers.

front: On which river is the Bhakra-Nangal multipurpose project constructed?
back: Sutlej River. The reservoir formed behind Bhakra Dam is Govind Sagar in Himachal Pradesh.

front: On which river is the Hirakud Dam, the longest earthen dam in India, built?
Which was the first multipurpose river valley project of independent India?
back: Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC), established in 1948 on the Damodar River, modeled on the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) in the USA.

front: Which river does the Kaleshwaram Lift Irrigation Project (KLIP) draw water from, and which is its primary barrage?
back: Godavari River. The primary intake barrage is the Medigadda (Lakshmi) Barrage at the confluence of the Godavari and Pranahita rivers.

front: On which river and district is the Sriram Sagar Project (SRSP / Pochampad) built?
back: Godavari River at Pochampad in Nizamabad district. It is considered the lifeline of North Telangana agriculture.

front: On which river is the Nagarjuna Sagar Project constructed?
back: Krishna River (border of Nalgonda district, Telangana and Palnadu/Guntur, AP). Foundation stone was laid on 10 December 1955 by Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru.

front: What is the water application efficiency of Drip Irrigation vs Sprinkler Irrigation?
back:
Drip Irrigation: ~90-95% efficiency (delivers water directly to root zone, prevents evaporation).
Sprinkler Irrigation: ~75-85% efficiency (simulates natural rainfall, suitable for undulating/sandy soils).

front: What are the 4 main components of PMKSY (Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana)?
back:
1. Accelerated Irrigation Benefit Programme (AIBP)
2. Har Khet Ko Pani
3. Per Drop More Crop (Micro-irrigation)
4. Watershed Development.
